extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduate / graduate students and researchers in commutative algebra
extracted.subtask_description: Statements, propositions and exercises about localization, supports of modules, the structure presheaf on Spec(A), the constructible topology, and primary decomposition in commutative algebra. Useful for understanding how localization, tensor, and prime-spectrum maps behave.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tensor distributes over direct sums
rubrics_metrics.description: For an A-module N and an arbitrary direct sum ⊕_{i∈I} M_i, the natural map N × ⊕ M_i → ⊕ (N ⊗ M_i) is bilinear and induces an isomorphism N ⊗ (⊕_{i} M_i) ≅ ⊕_{i} (N ⊗ M_i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof via universal property of tensor: check injectivity (if ˜f((n ⊗ m_i)_i)=0 then each n⊗m_i=0 so n=0 or all m_i=0) and surjectivity is clear. This is used to deduce S^{-1} commutes with arbitrary direct sums (apply with N = S^{-1}A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization commutes with arbitrary direct sums (Prop 3.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: For multiplicative S and modules M_i, S^{-1}(⊕_i M_i) ≅ ⊕_i S^{-1}M_i (as S^{-1}A-modules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct via tensor product fact above and the identification S^{-1}M ≅ S^{-1}A ⊗_A M; refer to Proposition 3.5 for formal statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization as a directed limit (Claim XIX)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given multiplicative S ⊆ A, ordering S by s ≤ t iff ∃u∈S with t = us makes S directed. For an A-module M, with M_s the localization at powers of s, the direct system (M_s, μ_{ij}) has direct limit lim_{s∈S} M_s ≅ S^{-1}M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define transition maps μ_{ij} via chosen t with j = it and check well-definedness and compatibility; construct maps α_s: M_s → S^{-1}M and use universal property of the direct limit to show α: lim M_s → S^{-1}M is an isomorphism (injectivity via clearing denominators, surjectivity obvious).

rubrics_metrics.name: Support of a finitely generated module equals V(Ann(M))
rubrics_metrics.description: If M is finitely generated by x_1,...,x_n and M ≅ ⊕ A x_i ≅ ⊕ A/a_i, then Supp(M) = ⋃ Supp(A/a_i) = ⋃ V(a_i) = V(∑ a_i). In particular ∑ a_i = Ann(M), so Supp(M) = V(Ann(M)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the canonical surjections A → A x_i and exercise references. Shows support of finitely generated modules is a Zariski-closed set V(I).

rubrics_metrics.name: Support of tensor product (Prop 3.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: For A-modules M,N one has Supp(M ⊗_A N) = Supp(M) ∩ Supp(N).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Localize at p: (M⊗N)_p ≅ M_p ⊗_{A_p} N_p. By Exercise 2.3 (tensor over local rings), M_p ⊗ N_p = 0 iff M_p = 0 or N_p = 0. Take contrapositive to get the equality of supports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support of quotient by a: M/aM
rubrics_metrics.description: Supp(M/aM) = Supp(A/a) ∩ Supp(M) = V(a) ∩ V(Ann(M)) = V(a ∪ Ann(M)) = V(a + Ann(M)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use isomorphism M/aM ≅ (A/a) ⊗_A M and previous properties of support under tensor and supports of cyclic modules; ideals containing a∪Ann(M) contain a+Ann(M).

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavior of support under base change (extension of scalars)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an A-algebra B and q a prime of B with preimage p in A, (B ⊗_A M)_q ≅ B_q ⊗_{A_p} M_p. Thus q ∈ Supp_B(B⊗_A M) iff p ∈ Supp_A(M) (so passing to B preserves/nonpreserves vanishing of stalks as described).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Proposition 3.5 and Exercise 2.15 to identify localizations and then tensor; apply finite-generation arguments (Corollary 2.13) for the converse direction when needed in proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prime correspondence for localization (Prop 3.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a bijection Spec(S^{-1}A) ↔ {p ∈ Spec(A) : p ∩ S = ∅} given by contraction/extension. Under this correspondence p^e c = (p:s) = p for p ∈ S^{-1}X, and contraction/extension behave compatibly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequences: the map φ*: Spec(S^{-1}A)→Spec(A) is a homeomorphism onto its image (continuous and closed); for S = {1,f,f^2,...} the image equals X_f, so Spec(A_f) identifies with X_f. Use these facts to manipulate basic opens and local pictures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatibility of localization with ring homomorphisms (functoriality diagram)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given f: A→B and multiplicative S in A, the diagram of induced maps between Spec(S^{-1}A), Spec(S^{-1}B), Spec(A), Spec(B) commutes; equivalently S^{-1}f: S^{-1}A → S^{-1}B satisfies the expected compatibilities on prime spectra.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check at representatives a/s and use that f(s) avoids primes in the image so denominators behave; used to show φ*-maps commute in base change diagrams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equality of basic open sets implies isomorphism of localizations
rubrics_metrics.description: If X_f = X_g as subsets of Spec(A) then A_f ≅ A_g as rings (and conversely when appropriate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses radicals r((f)) = r((g)) leading to f^n = h g and g^m = h' f etc.; use universal property of localization to construct inverses and show compositions are identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canonical localization and quotient maps are epimorphisms in Ring
rubrics_metrics.description: The natural projection A→A/a and the canonical map A→S^{-1}A are epimorphisms (right-cancellable morphisms) in the category of rings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For quotient this follows from surjectivity; for localization use that any two ring maps from S^{-1}A agreeing on A must agree on all fractions since images of s are invertible and inverses are unique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presheaf of rings on Spec: A(U) = S_U^{-1}A and stalks
rubrics_metrics.description: For U open in X = Spec(A) define S_U = A  igcup_{p∈U} p (saturated multiplicative set) and A(U) := S_U^{-1}A. Restriction maps ρ_{U,V} for V⊆U make U↦A(U) a presheaf; the stalk at x ∈ X is A_p. For U=X one gets A(X)≅A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check directedness for basic opens, compatibility of restriction maps (ρ_UU = id, ρ_UW = ρ_VW ◦ ρ_UV) and identify stalks via direct limits over neighborhoods. This constructs the structure presheaf (and with further checks becomes the structure sheaf).

rubrics_metrics.name: Gluing of sections for basic open covers (sheaf condition for structure presheaf)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a finite basic-open cover X = ⋃_{i=1}^n X_{f_i} and compatible local sections s_i ∈ A(X_{f_i}) that agree on overlaps, there is a unique global section s ∈ A(X) restricting to each s_i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Existence: construct s locally using a finite subcover argument with manipulations of powers of f_i and denominators; uniqueness: if two global sections agree on each X_{f_i} then their difference is killed by powers of the f_i and a linear combination argument shows difference is zero. This proves the sheaf gluing for finite basic covers (Exercise 3.23/3.24 style).

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructible topology τ defined via images of Specs
rubrics_metrics.description: Let τ be the topology generated by sets of the form f_*(Spec(B)) for ring maps f: A→B (i.e., images of spectra). The closed sets in τ are exactly such images; τ is finer than the Zariski topology because V(a)=Spec(A/a) image is of this form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Properties proved: τ is closed under arbitrary intersections and finite unions (via tensor products and direct products of rings), contains ∅ and Spec(A), and thus is a topology. It is in general finer than Zariski; basic sets X_g are clopen in τ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quasi-compactness and separation properties of constructible topology
rubrics_metrics.description: The constructible space X_C (Spec(A) with τ) is quasi-compact; X_C is Hausdorff and totally disconnected (each point is a connected component).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofs: quasi-compactness via finite generation and reducing to vanishing of tensor algebras; Hausdorffness by separating distinct primes with clopen X_f; compact Hausdorff + totally disconnected imply a Stone space. Continuity and homeomorphism arguments with identity map between Zariski and constructible topologies are used when A is absolutely flat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empty spectrum iff zero ring (Claim XXI)
rubrics_metrics.description: A commutative ring with unity has empty prime spectrum iff it is the zero ring. (Note: rings without 1 may behave differently.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If nonzero ring with 1 then by existence of maximal ideals (Theorem 1.3) Spec nonempty; converses discussed for rings without 1 by counterexamples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image of Spec under maps and behavior under filtered colimits (Ex. 27 and related)
rubrics_metrics.description: If B = colim_{α} B_α as A-algebras then f_*(Spec(B)) = ⋃_α f_{α*}(Spec(B_α)); finite tensor / product decompositions reduce image computations to finite cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use that Spec of a directed colimit is union of images of the finite pieces (tensor products/product decompositions) and Exercise references (2.20–2.23, 3.25, 3.26) to reduce general images to finite constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary decomposition: isolated components and second uniqueness theorem (Thm 4.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a = ∩_{i=1}^n q_i is a minimal primary decomposition and {p_{i1},...,p_{im}} is an isolated set of prime ideals of a, then the intersection q_{i1} ∩ ··· ∩ q_{im} is independent of the choice of minimal decomposition. Corollary: isolated primary components (those corresponding to minimal primes) are uniquely determined by a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses saturation S = A  igcup p_{ij} and Proposition 4.9 to show S(a) and hence the intersection are determined by a; relate to uniqueness of associated primes (Theorem 4.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Saturation S(a) properties (Prop 4.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given multiplicative S ⊆ A and ideal a, define S(a) = contraction of S^{-1}a: (1) S(a) = {x∈A : ∃ s∈S with s x ∈ a} = ⋂_{s∈S} (a : s) = a^{ec} ⊇ a. (2) S(0)=ker φ_S. (3) For S_p = A rak p and q p-primary, S_p(q)=q. (4) S_p(0) is contained in every p-primary ideal. (5) If S_1⊆S_2 then S_1(a)⊆S_2(a). (6) If b⊇a then S(a)⊆S(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each point proved by unraveling extension/contraction, localization facts, and simple inclusions; Claim XXII (extension and contraction preserve inclusion) underlies some steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension and contraction preserve order (Claim XXII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Both extension (a ↦ a^e) and contraction (b ↦ b^c) preserve inclusions of ideals: if a⊆b then a^e ⊆ b^e and similarly for contractions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate from definitions: generators/images behave monotonically; used repeatedly in saturation and localization arguments.
